chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Ishaq, from Al-Hasan ibn Hazm Al-Kalbi, the brother-in-law of Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever does not make his will well at the time of death, it is a deficiency in his honor and intellect."
It was said: O Messenger of Allah, how does the dying person make his will? He said: "When his death approaches and the people gather around him, he says:
"O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen," the Merciful, the Compassionate.

O Allah, I bequeath to You in the abode of the world that I bear witness that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, and that Paradise is true, and Hell is true, and the Resurrection is true, and the Reckoning is true, and Justice and Decree and the Balance are true, and that the Quran is true, and that the Quran is as You sent it down, and that You are Allah, the Clear Truth.
May Allah reward Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with the best reward, and may Allah give life to Muhammad and the family of Muhammad with peace.

O Allah, O my provision in my distress, O my companion in my hardship, O my guardian of my blessing, my God and the God of my fathers, do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, for if You leave me to myself, I would be closer to evil and further from good.
And make my loneliness in the grave familiar to me, and make for me a covenant on the Day I meet You, [when I am] displayed.
Then he makes his specific bequests.

And the confirmation of this will is in the Quran, in the Surah in which Maryam is mentioned, in His Exalted and Majestic saying: "They do not have the power of intercession except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful." (1)
This is the covenant of the dying person, and the will is obligatory upon every Muslim to memorize this will and teach it.

And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) taught it to me," and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Gabriel (peace be upon him) taught it to me."

And as for charity, it is your utmost effort until you say 'I have exceeded,' even if you have not exceeded. And upon you is the Night Prayer, and upon you is the Night Prayer, and upon you is the Night Prayer. And upon you is the Midday Prayer, and upon you is the Midday Prayer, and upon you is the Midday Prayer. And upon you is the recitation of the Quran in all states. And upon you is raising your hands in your prayer and turning them. And upon you is using the Siwak at every ablution and every prayer. And upon you is good character, so adopt it, and bad character, so avoid it. If you do not do so, do not blame anyone but yourself.

key_terms.السِّوَاكِ: Toothstick (for oral hygiene and ritual purity)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and will for a dying Muslim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni and cited in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, establishes the 'Will of the Dying' (Wasiyyat al-Mawt) as a crucial act of preserving one's intellectual and moral integrity (muruwah) at the moment of death. It links the spiritual efficacy of this testimony to Surah Maryam, verse 87, highlighting that divine intercession is reserved for those who have made a covenant with the Merciful, thereby elevating the personal declaration to a cosmic guarantee. The text further prescribes specific devotional practices—such as night prayers, midday prayers, and the use of the Siwak—as essential preparations for the soul's journey, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both ritual precision and ethical refinement.
